scope: Actual live-code pre-send guards and transaction identity/signing/broadcast retry boundaries. Final verification uses synthetic HTTP/RPC/orders and detached synthetic SDK keys only. An initial full-suite test fixture accidentally initialized the operator signer through lazy package getattr in the working checkout; it was replaced before any signing/broadcast method was called. No operator signing, wallet RPC query or real order is invoked.
findings: The live buyer treated an unavailable/failed Jupiter quote as (true, unknown impact) and treated Price API availability as a route. Required quote failures could reach execution.
The buyer queried a price-based route proxy for every buy, then fetched the required price again. This added redundant work and did not prove exact-size routing.
GMGN retried its entire buy/sell function, including re-routing and signing after a possibly successful submission. Outer buyer/seller no-retry guards did not prevent these inner retries.

The signing module imported VersionedTransaction from a module absent in the installed SDK, used message bytes without the v0 version prefix, and fell back to legacy attributes not provided by the installed Transaction class.

The legacy Transaction-object path refreshed/signature-mutated inside an RPC retry loop and expected a dictionary get_latest_blockhash response rather than the installed typed response. It could not safely preserve one transaction identity.
SOL/raw units were derived with separate binary-float multiplications in quote, funds and submission consumers. Transport and capital checks need the same exact boundary.
Broadcast responses were accepted without matching the first signature of the originally signed transaction. That is an acknowledgement identity check, not chain confirmation.

implementation.units: Share strict raw uint64 parsing and Decimal SOL-to-lamport flooring. Quotes, actual funds checks, managed buy inputs and GMGN buy inputs consume the same conversion. Invalid/sub-lamport inputs and unknown gas reserve cannot authorize a live buy. Exact 0.1 SOL remains 100000000 units.
implementation.pre_send: One actual request-bound quote is required by the existing Jupiter policy or the selected managed Jupiter venue. Recheck original raw quote identity/amount/mode/slippage/route/impact and its returned measured values. Missing router, malformed values, timeout or invalid impact limit are not permission. Invalid impact limits have a durable checked no-fill rejection. Cancellation propagates without submission.
implementation.venue_policy: Preserve the optional GMGN-only policy without adding a Jupiter veto or redundant Jupiter price/quote request. Keep the existing required Price API rule separate and reject nonfinite/bool/unknown price values. Select the canonical token_mint for the GMGN call. No admission threshold or paper runner upside ceiling is changed.
implementation.gmgn_retry: Remove retry decorators around buy and sell. Retry only the read-only route GET on bounded transient connection/timeout/5xx failures; do not retry forbidden/other 4xx, malformed JSON or cancellation. Once signing/sending begins, the wrapper never requests a fresh route or sends another order.
implementation.signing: Use the installed solders.transaction VersionedTransaction API for legacy/v0 bytes. Sign to_bytes_versioned at the actual configured required-signer index; preserve the original message, fee payer and other signatures. A managed provider may receive a partial signature, but local RPC broadcast requires all original signatures to verify. Reject a foreign wallet before broadcast.
implementation.legacy_object: For a supported single-configured-signer Transaction object, obtain one valid blockhash via the installed typed response or legacy dictionary compatibility before signing. Rebuild the same header/account/instruction layout without mutating the caller or changing fee payer; sign once, then all endpoints receive identical bytes. Never refresh or re-sign after any broadcast. Reject a blockhash refresh that would invalidate unavailable co-signatures.
implementation.acknowledgement: Require RPC/Jito acknowledgement to match the original first transaction signature. RPC dictionary errors and malformed/nonobject/error/unrelated Jito acknowledgements remain unknown. Jito-to-RPC or RPC endpoint relays preserve exactly the original packet, not a newly signed order.
implementation.key_compatibility: Parse complete JSON byte arrays including spaces and validate byte types/range. Preserve valid base58/base64 seed/key formats and reject malformed data; synthetic tests use detached modules and override signing/RPC credential environment values before loading. Paper cold imports remain keyless and never load the signing module.
